title.narrative: Sustaining and Improving the Gains for HIV and TB

description.narrative: Zambia - TB/HIV - Churches Health Association of Zambia - CHAZ. This program has the following goals: Reduce new HIV infections from 51,000 in 2019, by at least 50% by 2023. Reduce AIDS related mortality by 50% from 20,000 in 2019. Reduce HIV related stigma and discrimination by 50%. Mother to child transmission of HIV eliminated, from 3.7% in 2019 to less than 3%, by 2023. To reduce the number of TB deaths in the population by 40% in 2021 compared to 2015. The objectives of this program are: 95% of PLHIV know their HIV status. 1. Establish and maintain early warning and response surveillance platforms to address all health threats and health emergencies and natural disasters in a timely and effective manner 2.Support districts in health emergency responses 3. Harmonize disease control and prevention policies and the surveillance systems in the country 4. Support public health capacity-building through medium and long-term field epidemiology and laboratory training programs 5. support and/or conduct hazard mapping and risk assessments for districts 6. Evaluate and integrate information to determine Zambia’s population health status, set priorities, and suggest evidence-based interventions 7. Provide an integrated platform for information collection, collation and dissemination 8. support health promotion and disease prevention through health system strengthening by address infectious and non-communicable diseases, injuries, environmental health and Neglected Tropical diseases (NTDs) 9. Strengthen and establish laboratory capacity to diagnose priority zoonotic diseases and public health events at all provincial levels by 2026.. 95% of people diagnosed with HIV enrolled on ART. 95% of PLHIV receiving ART achieve viral suppression. To reduce stigma and discrimination associated with HIV and AIDS. To improve access and utilisation of HIV and AIDS servcies by population groups most at risk. To increase the treatment success rate for TB from 90% in 2019 to at least 95% from 2023 onwards
